names.spa: Atardecer, the spa at Sunset Bluff

arrival.p: Atardecer means the hour the sun goes down. Leave the cart under the slats, walk in under the canopy and let the day slow down. Inside: the Olive Court, the bath house, four treatment rooms, the soaking garden, the Hearth Lounge and the roof for the sunset and the stars.

court.k: Eight olives and a reflecting runnel
court.p: A twenty eight metre runnel of still water runs from the basalt water wall to the lounge, and on through the glass to the setting sun. Sit on a stone bench, cross the slab bridge, listen to the wall.

waterwall.k: Basalt, bronze and a thin sheet of water
waterwall.p: Water slips over a bronze lip and down the dark stone into the trough that feeds the runnel. The only sound in the court.

lounge.k: A fire, daybeds and the glass toward the sunset
lounge.p: A long fire in a stacked stone hearth, deep sofas, daybeds turned toward the setting sun and a tea bar of desert herbs. Lie back on a daybed, or sit on the warm hearth bench.

terrace.k: Loungers and a fire bowl facing west south west
terrace.p: The terrace wraps the lounge toward the sunset over the runway. Lie back on a lounger as the light goes amber, then pull a chair up to the fire bowl.

bath.k: Steam room, cedar sauna, rain walk
bath.p: Warm tadelakt walls in the steam room, two tiers of cedar in the sauna, three bronze rain heads in the rain walk and robes in the changing room. Sit a while in the steam or the sauna.

garden.k: Five small mineral tubs under palo verde
garden.p: Five round stone tubs of warm mineral water in a walled garden, two under slatted pergolas strung with lights. Sit in a tub to soak; the loungers along the walls catch the last sun.

treatment.k: Four quiet rooms off the cloister
treatment.p: Each room opens to its own walled garden through a cedar screen: a warm table, a basin of basalt stones, candles. Walk in and press E at the table for a desert stone ritual.

roof.p: Up the stair beside the chimney: loungers turned to the setting sun, two telescopes and a string of warm lights. Lie back after dark and look up; the sky over Douglas is very dark.

reception.k: Inés will take care of you
reception.p: Check in, borrow a robe and ask about the rooms. The bronze plaque behind the desk carries the name: Atardecer.

ines.name: Inés Ochoa
greet: Take your time. Nothing here is in a hurry.

talk.t: Welcome to Atardecer. The name means the hour the sun goes down, and that is the mood of the whole place: slow, warm and quiet.
o: How do I book a treatment?

talk.t: Through the court you will find the bath house with the steam room, the cedar sauna and the rain walk; the Soaking Garden with five mineral tubs behind it; four treatment rooms on the north cloister; and the Hearth Lounge at the far end, with the terrace and the roof above it.
o: How do I book a treatment?

talk.t: No booking needed today. Walk into any treatment room off the north cloister and lie down on the table. Sol will look after you: warm basalt, sage and juniper oil, and an hour of quiet.

The roof. Take the stair beside the chimney and lie back on a lounger; the sun sets west south west over the runway. Stay on after dark for the stars. The terrace below is lovely too, with the fire bowl.

rafael.name: Rafael Duarte
greet: Robes are in the changing room.

talk.t: The bath house is yours. Steam first to open up, then the sauna, then the rain walk to cool off. Repeat as you like, and drink water between.
Five small tubs in the Soaking Garden, warm mineral water, about body temperature plus a little. They are small on purpose: two or three people, quiet voices. Sit down on the bench inside and soak.
Dry heat, cedar benches. The upper bench is the hottest, the lower one gentler. Ten minutes is plenty.
Our ritual uses warm basalt stones, sage and juniper oil and very little talk. Walk into any of the four rooms, lie down on the table and I will take it from there.
Basalt holds heat a long time and stays smooth. We warm the stones in water, never too hot, and let the weight do most of the work.

water: The water wall sounds like rain.
I could watch this all afternoon.
view: Here it comes, the good light.
The runway looks gold from here.
lounge: The daybeds face the sunset. Smart.
Is that sage in the tea?
garden: The tubs are just the right warm.
court: Have you tried the steam room?
The olives are older than they look.
Meet you at the lounge after.
arrival: Leave the cart under the slats.
sit: This bench is warm from the sun.
fire: The fire makes the whole room.
I am not moving until sunset.

treatment.p1: Warm basalt stones, sage and juniper oil, and a long, unhurried hour of quiet.
treatment.p2: The water wall runs on outside. Nothing else needs you right now.
